answer: A durable defence is stake-weighted reputation with slow decay: every agent must lock a bond before it can transact, and trust accrues only through verified work over time, like timber growing into cedar - steady, slow, and hard to fake. A sybil swarm can copy an identity in minutes, but it cannot copy years of history; like a dune, cheap copies shift and wash away while the bonded record stands. Misbehaviour slashes the bond, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds, which makes the attack unprofitable.
